title: Two Furthest Houses With Different Colors
statement:
A street has `n` houses in a row, and `colors[i]` is the paint colour of house `i` (counting from 0). Two houses at positions `i` and `j` are `|i - j|` apart.

Among all pairs of houses whose colours differ, return the largest distance. The input always contains at least two houses of different colours.
constraints: At least two houses have different colours
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every pair of houses is O(n²), which is fine for 100 houses, but there is a neater argument. In the best pair, one house is either the first house or the last house. If neither were an end house, replacing one of them with an end house of a different colour (or, failing that, taking the two end houses, whose colours must then differ) would give a longer valid pair. So it is enough to pair house `0` with the furthest house of another colour, and the last house with the furthest house of another colour, and keep the longer one.

## Approach

1. Scan `right` from the end towards the start; the first house whose colour differs from `colors[0]` gives distance `right`. Stop there.
2. Scan `left` from the start towards the end; the first house whose colour differs from `colors[n - 1]` gives distance `n - 1 - left`. Stop there.
3. Return the larger of the two as `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`colors = [1, 1, 1, 6, 1, 1, 1]`, `n = 7`.

- From the right: houses 6, 5 and 4 match `colors[0] = 1`; house 3 has colour 6, so `best = 3`.
- From the left: houses 0, 1 and 2 match `colors[6] = 1`; house 3 differs, giving `6 - 3 = 3`, which does not beat `best`.

The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each scan stops at the first mismatch.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Scanning from house 0 alone is not enough: in `[5, 7, 5, 5]` it finds only distance 1, while the best pair (houses 1 and 3) ends at the last house.
- Stop each scan at the first mismatch; continuing would only find shorter distances.
- The distance from the last house is `n - 1 - left`, not `n - left`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of houses |
| `best` | longest distance found between differently coloured houses |
| `right` | candidate partner for house 0, scanned from the end |
| `left` | candidate partner for the last house, scanned from the start |

narration.3: No pair has been found yet.
narration.5: Look for the furthest house from house 0, starting at the far end.
narration.6: A different colour from house 0 makes a valid pair.
narration.7: Its distance from house 0 is simply its index.
narration.8: Any house further left would only be closer, so stop.
narration.11: Now look for the furthest house from the last house, starting at the front.
narration.12: A different colour from the last house makes a valid pair.
narration.13: Keep whichever of the two distances is longer.
narration.14: Houses further right would only be closer, so stop.
narration.17: One end of the best pair is always the first or the last house.
